voyage.name: Vegas Golden Knights (NHL)
voyage.address: T-Mobile Arena, 3780 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: NHL (ice hockey) team that made it all the way to the Stanley Cup Final in its first season in 2017–18 (though losing), and lifted the Cup in its sixth season in 2022–23. The city's first team in one of the "big four" professional sports of the US and Canada, joined by the Las Vegas Raiders of the NFL in 2020.

voyage.name: Las Vegas Raiders (NFL)
voyage.content: NFL (football) team that began playing in Las Vegas in 2020 after relocating from Oakland.

voyage.name: Las Vegas Aces
voyage.address: Michelob Ultra Arena, 3950 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: WNBA (women's basketball) team that relocated from San Antonio to Vegas in 2018. The arena is part of the Mandalay Bay casino resort.

voyage.name: Las Vegas Aviators
voyage.content: Triple-A baseball club, the Aviators have been in Las Vegas longer than any other professional sports team. The Aviators began as the Las Vegas Stars in 1983, changed their name to the Las Vegas 51s, a reference to Area 51, in 2001, and became the Aviators for 2019 and beyond. They have won 2 Pacific Coast League crowns and 10 division titles. The team opened a new ballpark in Summerlin in 2019.

voyage.name: Henderson Silver Knights
voyage.address: Lee’s Family Forum, 200 S Green Valley Pkwy, Henderson
voyage.content: The Golden Knights' top minor-league team, playing in the American Hockey League. They moved to the new Dollar Loan Center in Henderson shortly before the end of the 2021–22 season.

voyage.name: NASCAR
voyage.content: Las Vegas hosts NASCAR for a weekend every year, usually in March. The race draws about 150,000 race fans to the city. Many cheer for Vegas natives Kurt and Kyle Busch. Aside from NASCAR, the speedway hosts many other racing events throughout the year.

voyage.name: National Finals Rodeo
voyage.content: Arguably the city's most prominent sporting event is the finals of the annual Professional Rodeo Cowboys Association circuit, held over 10 days in December just off the Strip at the Thomas & Mack Center on the UNLV campus.

voyage.name: Professional Bull Riders World Finals
voyage.content: Another major rodeo event is the finals of the Professional Bull Riders series, a separate circuit dedicated to bull riding. The PBR finals, held in late October/early November at the T-Mobile Arena, have more of an international flavor than the NFR—while the NFR is exclusive to the US and Canada, PBR runs national series in Brazil, Canada, Mexico, and Australia, and all of these countries, especially Brazil, are rep

voyage.name: UNLV Rebels
voyage.content: The athletic teams of the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, better known as UNLV, are also popular in the area. The Rebels are members of the Mountain West Conference, which has 12 members in football and 11 members for other sports. The most famous UNLV team is the men's basketball team, known as the "Runnin' Rebels"; though not as strong as in their heyday from the late 1970s through the early 1990s, they remain sol

voyage.name: Las Vegas Ice Center
voyage.content: A twin-rink facility.

voyage.name: Bellagio Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
voyage.content: Inside of the casino is a display of trees and flower arrangements, changed once for every season and once for the Chinese New Year.

voyage.name: Fountains of Bellagio
voyage.hours: Mon–Fri every half hour from 3PM to 8PM and every 15 minutes from 8PM to midnight; Sat Sun and holidays every half hour from noon to 8PM and every fifteen minutes from 8PM to midnight
voyage.content: The Fountains of the Bellagio perform a magnificent display, set to music. If you have the time, it's worth staying for two or three shows, as it is not at all the same show every time.

voyage.name: Bellagio Gallery of Fine Art
voyage.price: General:$18. Seniors (65+), Students, Teachers, Military and Nevada Residents:$16. Children 12 and under:Free
voyage.hours: 10AM-8PM. May change due to private functions
voyage.content: A fine-art gallery. See website for current exhibition.

voyage.name: Madame Tussauds
voyage.content: The only celebrity wax attraction on the Strip, featuring wax recreations of 100+ celebrities and famous figures.

voyage.name: Flamingo Garden
voyage.content: A 15-acre garden with flamingos and other exotic birds, as well as koi and turtles.

voyage.name: Eiffel Tower Experience
voyage.price: Evening: $16.50 adults, $11.50 children/seniors; daytime: $11.50 adults, $7.50 children/seniors
voyage.address: Paris Las Vegas, 3655 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: You can take an elevator to the top of the Eiffel Tower on the Strip, a half-sized replica of the one in Paris. This is a popular attraction, especially at night, for its excellent views of the Strip.

voyage.name: Shark Reef Aquarium at Mandalay Bay
voyage.hours: Sun-Thu 10AM-8PM, Fri Sat 10AM-10PM; summer hours daily 10AM-10PM
voyage.content: The highlight is walking through a transparent tunnel with sharks, sea turtle, fish on all sides.

voyage.name: Welcome to Fabulous Las Vegas sign
voyage.content: Possibly the most famous of Las Vegas' many signs, this landmark welcomes visitors getting in from the south along the Strip. And even if one has arrived into Las Vegas some other way, it's still very popular to go there and take photos and selfies of the sign.

voyage.name: Stripper 101
voyage.content: Pole dancing classes. For ladies aged 18 and over only. Advanced booking required. Pole provided.

voyage.name: The Twilight Zone by Monster Mini Golf
voyage.content: Glow-in-the-dark Twilight Zone–themed miniature golf, on an indoor course illuminated by black (ultraviolet) lights. Good for kids.

voyage.name: Vegas Indoor Skydiving
voyage.content: Fly your body in a vertical wind tunnel. No experience necessary, all training and equipment provided. Safe for all ages.

voyage.name: High Roller
voyage.price: Online tickets: $29 daytime, $39 nighttime, family/group options available
voyage.address: 3545 S Las Vegas Blvd, The LINQ
voyage.content: Opened in April 2014, this is the world's tallest Ferris wheel at 550 feet. One revolution lasts between 30 and 45 minutes in an enclosed cabin with excellent views of the Strip.

voyage.name: Adventuredome Theme Park
voyage.price: Day pass $31.95. Under 48 in:$17.95. Individual rides: $6-12
voyage.content: America's 2nd largest indoor theme park with 25 rides and attractions for all ages.

voyage.name: Big Apple Coaster
voyage.content: A roller coaster that lifts riders up 203 ft, then drops down 144 ft, reaching speeds of . Simulates a jet fighter's barrel roll, with a 180° turn, a section that leaving riders hanging in the air, then twists and dives.

voyage.name: Gondola rides
voyage.price: $18.95 for 15 minutes on four-seat gondola; private two-person gondolas $75.80 (reservations may be made at the Emporio D'Gondola in the Grand Canal Shoppes)

voyage.name: MSG Sphere at The Venetian
voyage.content: A one-of-a-kind spherical theatre that hosts musical performances, unique films, and other shows.

voyage.name: Circus Circus
voyage.content: Aerialists, jugglers, acrobats and trapeze artists take the stage at the world's largest permanent circus daily. Expect standing room only at most times.

voyage.name: Mystère
voyage.address: Treasure Island, 3300 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: A classic Cirque show, full of amazing feats, impressive costumes, and humor. Definitely worth the time and money. Although it's family-friendly, it verges on too intense and psychedelic for younger children, so consider avoiding for children who are under eight.

voyage.name: "O"
voyage.content: The stage at the Bellagio contains a 1.5-million gallon swimming pool, from which most performers emerge and retreat to. It's an incredibly impressive show.

voyage.name: KÀ
voyage.address: MGM Grand, 3799 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: Spectacular show that tells a tale of imperial twins on a journey to fulfill their destinies. Runs for 90 minutes.

voyage.name: Michael Jackson One
voyage.address: Mandalay Bay, 3950 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: A tribute to the King of Pop.

voyage.name: Absinthe
voyage.address: Caesars Palace, 3570 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: A carnival themed mix of comedy, acrobats, and provocative performances. Filled with blue comedy, not for the timid. Adults only.

voyage.name: Blue Man Group
voyage.content: The silent Blue Men perform all sorts of experimental music on unconventional instruments.

voyage.name: Comedy Pet Theater
voyage.content: Extraordinary talents of performing pets. Highly entertaining for children.

voyage.name: ROUGE
voyage.address: The STRAT Theater, The STRAT Hotel, 2000 Las Vegas Blvd S
voyage.content: Adults-only (18+, photo ID required) cabaret and variety show combining burlesque-style dance, acrobatics and comedy.

voyage.name: Tournament of Kings
voyage.content: A medieval themed dinner show featuring knights, horses, swordfights, and other performances.

voyage.name: V - The Ultimate Variety Show
voyage.content: Includes magic, special effects, death-defying stunts, wild comedy, visual artists.

voyage.name: Vegas! The Show
voyage.address: Planet Hollywood, 3663 Las Vegas Blvd S
voyage.content: A trip back to the swank days of Frank, Dino and Sammy features a tap dance number, a tribute to Gladys Knight and a performance of the Can-Can.

voyage.name: Hitzville The Show
voyage.address: V Theater, Planet Hollywood, 3663 Las Vegas Blvd S, Ste. 360
voyage.content: Includes the Motown hits of Gladys Knight & The Pips, The Temptations, Tina Turner, The Four Tops and Motown diva Diana Ross & The Supremes as they rock the stage.

voyage.name: David Copperfield
voyage.content: One of the world's most famous magicians. Some of his best known illusions are making the Statue of Liberty disappear, walking through the Great Wall of China and flying over the audience (which he does nightly).

voyage.name: Nathan Burton Comedy Magic
voyage.content: Comedy and magic, family friendly.

voyage.name: Mat Franco - Magic Reinvented Nightly
voyage.hours: nightly 7PM and 9:30PM except Wed and Thu
voyage.content: Family friendly comedy and magic in an intimate setting from winner of America’s Got Talent Season 9.

voyage.name: The Mac King Comedy Magic Show
voyage.content: A family-friendly afternoon comedy magic show in Las Vegas, where Mac King, in his trademark plaid suit, mixes goofy, self-deprecating humor with clever close-up and audience-participation tricks.

voyage.name: Fantasy
voyage.content: Vocalist Lorena Peril takes center stage. Steamy choreography and striking vocals fused with a touch of comedy. The high-energy production show features a variety of performances including salsa, belly dancing routine and celebrity impersonations by comedian Sean E. Cooper.

voyage.name: X Burlesque
voyage.content: Showcases a variety of performances by six gorgeous dancers set to contemporary music. Combines high-energy performance with the use of props such as bathtubs, guitars, lollipops and feather boas.

voyage.name: Vegas Golden Knights
voyage.address: T-Mobile Arena, 3780 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: NHL (ice hockey) team that made it all the way to the Stanley Cup Final in its first season in 2017–18 (though losing), and lifted the Cup in 2023. The city's first team in one of the "big four" professional sports of the US and Canada, they have quickly established a devoted fanbase in the Las Vegas area.

voyage.name: Las Vegas Aces
voyage.address: Michelob Ultra Arena, 3950 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: WNBA (women's basketball) team that began play in Vegas in 2018, after having relocated from San Antonio. Their arena is part of the Mandalay Bay casino/resort complex.

voyage.name: Las Vegas Raiders
voyage.content: NFL (Football) team that began playing in Las Vegas in 2020 after relocating from Oakland.

voyage.name: Professional Bull Riders World Finals
voyage.content: The finals of the Professional Bull Riders series, a rodeo circuit devoted exclusively to bull riding. This isn't the only contrast with the city's other major rodeo event, the National Finals Rodeo held at UNLV's Thomas & Mack Center. Unlike the NFR, which is exclusive to the US and Canada, the PBR finals, held in late October/early November at the T-Mobile Arena since 2015, have more of an international flavor. PBR

voyage.name: Lockdown Escape Rooms - Highland
voyage.content: Three themed rooms for 2-8 players: Hostage Rescue, Mob Boss, and Crazy Professor rated from easy to medium difficulty.

voyage.name: Xterious Escape
voyage.content: Six escape rooms for 2-10 in five flavors can be found here: Casino's Dark 11, Code 13, Bugsy's Nightmare, Curse of Mapuche, and two identical versions of The Great Escape to allow teams to compete against each other.

voyage.name: Fashion Show Mall
voyage.content: Offers nearly every major and deluxe U.S. retail chain store, numerous others often associated with named designers, a large food court and several excellent restaurants, all in a fully-enclosed, air-conditioned facility. Has extensive, free covered parking that often gets quite busy by mid-day.

voyage.name: Forum Shops
voyage.content: A huge high-end shopping area that also offers free animatronics shows at Fountain of the Gods and Atlantis located at either end of the mall.

voyage.name: Grand Canal Shoppes
voyage.content: Another massive shopping area that features the tacky objets d'art shop featured in Martin Bashir's interview with Michael Jackson.

voyage.name: Miracle Mile Shops
voyage.content: Another large shopping area with approximately 150 stores and restaurants.

voyage.name: LinQ Promenade
voyage.content: A smaller promenade (at least in comparison to the others), but it contains a fair share of stores and restaurants, as well as the world's largest Ferris Wheel, the High Roller.

voyage.name: The Buffet
voyage.content: 16 exhibition cooking stations and a luxurious selection of extraordinary dishes. Dress is casual. Breakfast, lunch and dinner served, with champagne brunch on weekends.

voyage.name: The Buffet
voyage.content: Arguably the best buffet on the Strip, with the dinner menu including pre-split crab legs, venison, Kobe beef, and wild boar. Gourmet Friday dinner includes Beef Wellington, Rack of Lamb, Veal Ossobuco, Grilled Swordfish, and Curried Duck Legs. The Buffet has spectacular selections from Italy, China, and Japan as well as fresh seafood and traditional American food. Wait to enter can be 90 minutes or more.

voyage.name: Ocean One
voyage.price: $5.99 for each lunch option; $10–20 for dinner
voyage.content: Surprisingly inexpensive lunches for a restaurant on the strip. Not fine dining by any means, but a filling and tasty meal if you're trying not to break the bank.

voyage.name: Eggslut
voyage.content: Breakfast sandwiches made with farm-fresh eggs and a delicious brioche bun. Expect a 45 minute line on weekend mornings.

voyage.name: Hash House A Go Go
voyage.content: American food with enormous servings—two or three people can easily share an order. Has a few locations, including one on the strip, one downtown, and a couple further out.

voyage.name: Jimmy Buffett's Margaritaville
voyage.content: A fun tropical-themed restaurant featuring dishes named after many of Jimmy Buffett's songs (for example: the Cheeseburger in Paradise). At happy hour from 5-6PM they have beer for $0.05.

voyage.name: Amalfi by Bobby Flay
voyage.address: Caesars Palace, 3570 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: With a brightly colored decor and festive atmosphere, chef Bobby Flay serves us some tasty Southwestern food with flair.

voyage.name: Mon Ami Gabi
voyage.address: Paris Las Vegas, 3655 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: Nice restaurant serving mostly steaks and seafood. The staff makes a tribute to the restaurant's location by talking with French accent.

voyage.name: Peppermill Fireside Lounge
voyage.content: 1970s space-age decor and waitresses that call you 'hon'.

voyage.name: Strip House
voyage.content: Prime cuts of beef, sides, an extensive wine list and desserts based on the New York Strip House.

voyage.name: The Steak House
voyage.address: Circus Circus, 2880 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: Considered to be a hidden gem, The Steak House at Circus Circus doesn't seem fit in with its surroundings; indeed, it has been consistently voted one of the best steaks in Las Vegas for over twenty years. Beautiful decor, outstanding food, and impeccable service, as well as an extensive wine list.

voyage.name: Craftsteak
voyage.address: MGM Grand, 3799 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: Considered to be one of the best steak houses in America.

voyage.name: L'Atelier de Joël Robuchon
voyage.address: MGM Grand, 3799 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: Sophisticated French Michelin-starred restaurant with dim lighting, ruby red furniture, and spectacular food.

voyage.name: Momofuku
voyage.content: This is the Las Vegas entry of Michelin star-awarded chef David Chang, serving his inventive take on ramen noodle soup and other Asian inspired dishes.

voyage.name: Casa Fuente Cigars
voyage.address: Caesars Palace, 3500 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: Cuban-themed lounge offering more than 100 different cigars and a good selection of whiskeys. Try the $40 Opus X cigar.

voyage.name: Nine Fine Irishmen
voyage.address: New York-New York, 3790 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: This pub was constructed in Ireland and then shipped to Las Vegas. A great Irish band plays most nights starting around 9PM, the crowd is always energetic, and the Guinness and Bass flow easily.

voyage.name: Showgirl Bar
voyage.address: Planet Hollywood, 3663 S Las Vegas Blvd

voyage.name: Skyfall
voyage.address: Delano at Mandalay Bay, 3950 Las Vegas Fwy
voyage.content: Skyfall, on the 64th floor atop the Delano Hotel at Mandalay Bay, offers guests views of the Strip and the Las Vegas Valley from its floor-to-ceiling windows and terraces.

voyage.name: Tao Nightclub
voyage.price: $20-30 per drink. Part of the Tao Group
voyage.address: The Venetian Resort, 3377 South Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: One of the oldest and smallest nightclubs on the Las Vegas Strip. Often plays a hybrid of top 40, rap, and hip hop.

voyage.name: XS
voyage.address: Encore Las Vegas,3131 Las Vegas Blvd S
voyage.content: At the time of opening, the most expensive nightclub in the world. Known for Sunday nightswim pool parties, and features a hybrid indoor-outdoor setup. XS and its sister club Encore Beach Club most frequently book millennial-level EDM artists, with their most well known residents being Diplo, the Chainsmokers, and Marshmello.

voyage.name: Encore Beach Club at Night
voyage.hours: Most commonly opens Wed Sat at 10:30PM, though occasionally will open on other days
voyage.address: Encore Las Vegas, 3131 Las Vegas Blvd S
voyage.content: A nighttime pool party located at the primarily day-centric Encore Beach Club. Part of Wynn Nightlife, EBC hosts many of the same residents as Wynn

voyage.name: LIV
voyage.hours: Opens at 10PM on Fri, Sat, and Sun
voyage.address: Fontainebleau Las Vegas, 2777 S Las Vegas Blvd
voyage.content: The newest nightclub on the Las Vegas Strip, and has had a trend of booking headliners which appeal to Generation Z more so than the other nightclubs on the Strip. LIV frequently markets its kinetic lighting display above the dance floor as the "halo". LIV most commonly books new EDM talent, though occasionally hosts rappers such as 50 Cent.

voyage.name: Zouk
voyage.address: Resorts World, 3000 South Las Vegas Boulevard
voyage.content: An offshoot of the famous Singapore nightclub, Zouk features a mix of talent and performers on residency, such as James Hype, Don Toliver, Lil Jon, and Allison Wonderland.

voyage.name: Omnia
voyage.price: $20-30 per drink. Part of the Tao Group
voyage.address: Caesars Palace, 3570 S Las Vegas Boulevard
voyage.content: Perhaps one of the most recognizable clubs on the Strip after its appearance in the movie F1, Omnia is also one of the few clubs that almost never offers an open bar. Omnia is routinely an EDM center, opening its main room to host well-known headliners on Tuesday, Friday, and Saturday, though on Thursdays, it restricts its opening to only one of its smaller Heart of Omnia lounge, or to its rooftop terrace, preferring

voyage.name: Marquee
voyage.price: $20-30 per drink. Part of the Tao Group
voyage.address: The Cosmopolitan, 3708 S Las Vegas Boulevard
voyage.content: Renovated, Marquee regularly hosts EDM, though on Wednesdays, host niche house brands in a smaller room nicknamed "Lowkey in the Library". Marquee's most recurring residents are Cedric Gervais, Dmitri Vegas, and Chris Lake.

voyage.name: Jewel
voyage.price: $20-30 per drink. Part of the Tao Group
voyage.content: A smaller nightclub, Jewel is a common home for hip hop DJs on the Vegas Strip.

voyage.name: Hakkasan
voyage.price: $20-30 per drink. Part of the Tao Group
voyage.address: MGM Grand, 3799 S Las Vegas Boulevard
voyage.content: One of the most well-known nightlife spots in Las Vegas, Hakkasan traditionally hosts smaller R&B nights inside of its lounge level on Wednesdays, while opening up its main room on Thursdays for EDM, Fridays for Hip Hop, and Saturdays for EDM. Well known as one of the most common homes of Steve Aoki and Pauly D, alongside Tyga and Twinsick.

voyage.name: Howard Johnson on East Tropicana
voyage.content: Has a pool, free wifi, lots of parking and nearby to several bus stops.

voyage.name: OYO Hotel & Casino
voyage.content: Located behind the Tropicana and a quick walk to the Strip or monorail.

voyage.name: Artisan Hotel
voyage.content: A small non-gaming boutique hotel, popular among younger crowds seeking a vibrant night scene.

voyage.name: The Horseshoe
voyage.content: A moderate hotel and casino, but the location at the center of the Strip and the large rooms makes it one of the best values around.

voyage.name: Circus Circus
voyage.content: A cheaper and less upscale casino that caters to families. The Manor Motor Lodge is in poor shape; the Tower rooms are somewhat better.

voyage.name: Excalibur
voyage.content: Named after the mythical sword of King Arthur, this family friendly hotel has a large pool and rides for the kids.

voyage.name: Flamingo
voyage.content: A pink-colored resort in the middle of the Strip, the Flamingo was one of the first casinos on the Las Vegas Strip, and is famous for being owned by Bugsy Siegel.

voyage.name: Park MGM
voyage.content: Modeled after the opulent Place du Casino in Monte Carlo. Non-smoking casino and hotel.

voyage.name: Westin Las Vegas
voyage.content: 826 rooms and suites offer understated style. Non-smoking.

voyage.name: The Linq
voyage.content: Until 2012 known as the Imperial Palace and briefly known as The Quad. It has been refurbished and is surrounded by many forms of entertainment. The Linq Hotel offers access to the High Roller and Brooklyn Bowl, a nightlife bowling alley with live music. It also has many lounges, sports bars, and restaurants. In addition to the usual game tables, slot machines and restaurants, the Linq also hosts a car museum and the

voyage.name: Luxor Resort and Casino
voyage.content: An Egyptian-themed hotel with a massive pyramid that offers interesting room layouts. This hotel is a good option for those looking for a lower-priced but still upscale room on the Strip.

voyage.name: SAHARA Las Vegas
voyage.content: A boutique hotel and casino with over 1,600 guest rooms and suites, gaming, two pools, and diverse restaurant and nightlife options.

voyage.name: Trump International Hotel
voyage.content: 64 floors. Sweeping panoramic views of the city. 1,232 suites and 50 penthouse suites, complete with floor-to-ceiling windows. The Spa at Trump and Health Club.

voyage.name: Wynn Las Vegas & Encore Las Vegas
voyage.content: Built at a cost of $2.7 billion, this is the most expensive resort in the world, with the money plowed into (among other things) a private golf course, an artificial mountain with a 5-story waterfall and a million-gallon water tank for the nightly show.

voyage.name: The Venetian
voyage.content: A high-end hotel located near the center of the Strip and offering everything from the Grand Canal shops to shows and connected to the Palazzo complex. Rooms are spacious with high quality furnishings although no coffee/tea making facilities and it can be a long walk from your room to facilities. Plumbing occasionally questionable (noise and temperature).

voyage.name: Planet Hollywood Resort
voyage.content: 2,500 rooms, 2 swimming pools, casino, spa, fitness center, shops, 24-hour room service, free parking, restaurants and bars.

voyage.name: Caesars Palace
voyage.content: Renowned for its originality and features, Caesars Palace offers 3,300 hotel rooms and more than 26 different restaurants and cafes.

voyage.name: The Cromwell
voyage.content: Renovated in 2014, a luxury boutique hotel on the Strip. Features gambling and a rooftop pool with dayclub/nightclub. 188 rooms.

voyage.name: Bellagio
voyage.content: One of the most upscale hotels in Las Vegas, the Bellagio features an art gallery, a massive indoor flower garden, and the Cirque du Soleil show "O". One thing to do at the Bellagio (you do not have to stay there) is to have afternoon tea at the Petrossian Bar; it costs around $32 per person and is very classy, but you have to book at least a day in advance.

voyage.name: Paris Las Vegas
voyage.content: A hotel casino with over 2,900 rooms and large gaming floor that replicates a pleasant Parisian atmosphere.

voyage.name: Aria
voyage.content: Two hotel towers, nine bars, 17 restaurants, 1,840-seat theater, gift shop, 800,000 square foot spa, pool and 300,000 square feet of meeting space.

voyage.name: Waldorf Astoria Las Vegas
voyage.content: The most luxurious, nongaming hotel in CityCenter. 47 floors. The guest rooms and public spaces give off a feeling of class.

voyage.name: Cosmopolitan
voyage.content: Spectacular views and ultra-chic decor define the Cosmopolitan. The new 2,995-room resort features residential-style living spaces with expansive private terraces.

voyage.name: MGM Grand
voyage.content: Opened in 1993, this Hollywood themed resort has 5,044 guest rooms, 6.6 acres of swimming area, 2 wedding chapels, 3 theaters, multitudes of restaurants, a spa and salon, a 380,000-square-foot conference center, shops galore, and 165,000 square feet of casino floor.

voyage.name: Mandalay Bay
voyage.content: Located at the far southern end of the Strip next to the Luxor.

voyage.name: Four Seasons
voyage.content: Occupying the top four floors of Mandalay Bay's main building, the Four Seasons is one of the most high-end accommodations in Las Vegas.

voyage.name: Fremont Street Experience
voyage.content: A pedestrian mall lined by many of the downtown casinos, this is Las Vegas Downtown's equivalent of the Strip. Multimedia shows are displayed on a giant canopy over the street nightly.

voyage.name: The Tank at the Golden Nugget Hotel
voyage.content: A huge outdoor pool complex with a shark tank, a 3-story enclosed waterslide which passes through the shark tank, and private cabanas above the pool.

voyage.name: Urinals at Main Street Station Casino
voyage.content: The urinals in the men's room are mounted on an actual piece of the Berlin Wall. If you're a woman, ask an employee to let you see it, they almost always will accommodate you.

voyage.name: Container Park
voyage.content: A unique open-air shopping center filled with boutique retail shops, restaurants, and live entertainment for the whole family. Be sure to see the giant fire-breathing mantis at night.

voyage.name: Discovery Children's Museum
voyage.hours: Winter: Tue–Fri 9AM–4PM, Sat 10AM–5PM, Sun noon–5PM; Summer: Mon–Sat 10AM – 5PM, Sun noon–5PM
voyage.content: A combination museum and playground, this museum lets children engage in creative play while exposing them to science concepts. Kids especially love the 70-foot-tall Summit tower with 12 levels of interactive exhibits. The one drawback of the museum is lack of food; it's in a remote part of Downtown with no nearby eateries and only has a snack area with vending machines so plan accordingly.

voyage.name: Mob Museum
voyage.alt: National Museum of Organized Crime and Law Enforcement
voyage.price: $29.95 adults, $27.95 military/law enforcement, $16.95 children/students, children 10 and under free; discounts for Nevada residents
voyage.content: Extensive exhibits on the history of organized crime in the U.S., with lots of artifacts from famous mobsters and the law enforcement agencies that fought them. The museum is inside the old federal courthouse building, and includes a recreation of the courtroom where a major hearing on organized crime took place in 1950.

voyage.name: Neon Museum
voyage.content: An outdoor lot loaded with huge signs that once twinkled in front of the Silver Slipper, Stardust, and El Cortez. See the giant horseshoe made of thousands of gold-colored light bulbs. Open only by one-hour guided tours.

voyage.name: Old Las Vegas Mormon Fort State Historic Park
voyage.content: One of the few historic attractions in Vegas is this small park which preserves the restored Mormon Fort, the first structure built by European settlers in Las Vegas. A visitor center on-site has exhibits on the fort's past.

voyage.name: Las Vegas Natural History Museum
voyage.price: Adults $10; seniors, military, and students $8; children (3-11) $5

voyage.name: Stratosphere Tower
voyage.price: Elevator to the top: $20 adults, $12 children, $14 seniors/Nevada residents
voyage.content: A 1,149 foot high tower, the tallest observation tower in the United States, with an indoor and an outdoor observation deck on top that offers a 360-degree view over the valley. A revolving restaurant also sits at the top, as well as a set of thrill rides (see below in "Do").

voyage.name: Las Vegas Lights FC
voyage.address: Cashman Field, 850 Las Vegas Blvd N
voyage.content: A professional soccer team in the USL Championship league, the Las Vegas Lights have played at Cashman Field since 2018.

voyage.name: Mike Hammer
voyage.content: Comedy and magic.

voyage.name: Bite
voyage.content: Production show with vampire mythology and topless dancers.

voyage.name: SlotZilla
voyage.content: A zip line which stands 12 stories high and resembles a giant slot machine. Riders start at the east side of the Fremont Street Experience, the Slotzilla zip line is 114 feet high and launches riders in a horizontal position flying 1,700 feet — the entire length of the Fremont Street canopy – at speeds faster than 35 miles per hour. Up to four riders can ride at once, each on parallel zip lines.

voyage.name: Stratosphere Tower rides
voyage.price: Tower admission + Big Shot/X-Scream/Insanity rides $25-$36, depending on number of rides (otherwise, rides $15 each in addition to Tower admission); SkyJump $120 and up
voyage.content: In addition to the observation desk on top, with its restaurant and great views of the city, there are four thrill rides on the top of the tower. Big Shot is a tower ride that makes up the mast of the Stratosphere and shoots passengers straight up 160 feet at 45 mph (over 4 Gs) until they are 1,081 feet above the ground. X-Scream is a giant teeter-totter that propels you 27 feet over the edge of the tower, 866 feet a

voyage.name: Smith Center for the Performing Arts
voyage.content: Located in downtown Las Vegas, the Smith Center is a world-class performing arts center consisting of three theaters in two buildings. Visitors can attend regular concerts, popular musicals, and theatrical performances almost any day or night of the week. Online ticket reservations are recommended for better seating.

voyage.name: Las Vegas Premium Outlets North
voyage.content: 120 designer and name-brand outlets including Coach, Lacoste, Polo Ralph Lauren and more.

voyage.name: Gamblers Book Club
voyage.content: This is the oldest gambling book store in the nation; if you need to learn how to play a game, this is where you go. This store is stacked with books that can teach you how to count cards and bet on sports. Try to visit when former owner Howard Schwartz is around for some interesting Vegas lore.

voyage.name: Sin City Gallery
voyage.hours: Wed-Sat 1-7PM and opened until 10PM every first Thursday and first Friday of the month for First Fridays Arts Festival
voyage.content: Contemporary art gallery presenting sophisticated and edgy emerging artists from around the corner and around the world. Offers new exhibitions/murals every month. Sin City Gallery produces an international annual juried erotic art exhibition.

voyage.name: Oscar's Steakhouse
voyage.hours: Lounge opens at 4PM, restaurant at 5PM, Daily
voyage.content: Fine dining in the iconic Plaza Hotel and Casino. Named after former Las Vegas mayor and mob lawyer, Oscar Goodman.

voyage.name: Triple George Grill
voyage.content: Classic menu of seafood, chicken, steak and pasta.

voyage.name: Golden Steer Steakhouse
voyage.content: Open since 1958, this is the oldest steakhouse in Las Vegas and boasts to be one of favorite restaurants of Frank Sinatra, Dean Martin, and Sammy Davis Jr. and has hosted dinners for many other celebrities from past eras. The Golden Steer is over 50 years old and honors "Old Las Vegas" style dining.

voyage.name: Top of the World
voyage.content: A revolving gourmet restaurant more than 800 feet above the Strip at the top of the Stratosphere Tower.

voyage.name: Luv-It Frozen Custard
voyage.content: Hidden some two blocks north of the Stratosphere Tower (their blue building with white pillars and trim shares a parking lot with a convenience store), this family operation offers excellent frozen custards with outstanding toppings.

voyage.name: The Bunkhouse Saloon
voyage.content: Cheap downtown bar with live music. Friendly with travelers and frequented often by the staff and guests of the nearby hostel.

voyage.name: The Griffin
voyage.content: Old School Las Vegas ambience.

voyage.name: The Desert Hills Motel
voyage.content: Offers a variety of stylish deluxe suites, as well as standard accommodations. Amenities include a swimming pool, patio deck and large palm trees.

voyage.name: El Cortez Hotel and Casino
voyage.content: 300 rooms, 2 restaurants and a Chinese buffet. The right place to stay if you want to be in a memory of the past that's fading. Great rewards program.

voyage.name: Four Queens Hotel & Casino
voyage.content: No resort fees.

voyage.name: Golden Gate Hotel and Casino
voyage.content: Opened in 1906 under the name Hotel Nevada, this is the oldest casino hotel in Las Vegas.

voyage.name: Hostel Cat
voyage.content: Basic accommodations. Laundry and kitchen facilities, free pancake breakfast, wi-fi, some private rooms, lots of social activities.

voyage.name: Las Vegas Hostel
voyage.content: A definite budget option. A reasonably well kept hostel with very friendly staff. Free beer and BBQ at the weekend is not to be missed. Surrounding area is not overly safe. Walking alone at night is not recommended. The pizza parlor next door does a deal on a soda and a generous slice of pizza for around $3. Fremont Experience is roughly a 20-minute walk from the hostel.

voyage.name: Sin City Hostel
voyage.content: Hostel located near the north end of the Strip. Simple, clean, efficient. $15 per night in a 6-bed dorm includes continental breakfast.

voyage.name: California Hotel and Casino
voyage.content: No resort fees. Usually, a lot of the guests are Hawaiians, but everyone is welcome. Staff wears Aloha shirts and the buffet features Hawaiian specialties. Craps tables are usually lively, and they've got a "Golden Arm" hall of fame for craps shooters who've had an unusual hot streak. Give the big Buddha statue in the lobby a quick belly rub for luck before you play.

voyage.name: The D Las Vegas
voyage.content: A downtown casino right between the Fremont Street Experience and Slotzilla. Extensively renovated in 2012.

voyage.name: Downtown Grand Las Vegas
voyage.content: Stylish hotel rooms with modern amenities and comfortable furnishings. The industrial chic casino features brand new slot machines and table games in a high-energy and intimate environment.

voyage.name: Fremont Hotel & Casino
voyage.content: 32,000 square foot casino and 4 restaurants. No resort fees.

voyage.name: Main Street Station Hotel and Casino
voyage.content: Victorian theme. Includes not-to-be-missed Garden Court Buffet. No resort fees.

voyage.name: Stratosphere
voyage.content: Includes the 1,149-foot Stratosphere Tower, a Las Vegas landmark.

voyage.name: Springs Preserve
voyage.price: $18.95 adults, $17.05 seniors/students, $10.95 youth (discounts for Nevada residents and active military)
voyage.content: A large complex in the center of the city that features a Desert Living Center, interactive wildlife shows, galleries, museums, various gardens, and historical and nature trails.

voyage.name: Nevada State Museum, Las Vegas
voyage.price: Adults $19.95, Nevada Residents $9.95, Children 18 & under free

voyage.name: Las Vegas Chinatown Plaza
voyage.content: Chinatown Plaza is where Chinatown in Las Vegas was born and designated as Chinatown in 1996. The Mall is a place to experience Asian culture, baked goods, dim sum, and an Asian market are available to explore. Throughout the year the mall hosts various cultural events such as Lunar New year. Since then the area have grown to include 20+ other surrounding strip malls with a wide range of businesses, including restaur

voyage.name: Hollywood Cars Museum
voyage.price: $20 per person; kids under 16 are free with a paid adult. Cash only
voyage.content: A 30,000 square foot car museum featuring vehicles that have appeared in over 100 films and TV shows. Visitors can see, among others, several James Bond cars, Knight Rider's KITT, Batmobiles, and a Back to the Future Delorean.

voyage.name: Liberace Garage
voyage.price: Included with Hollywood Cars Museum ticket
voyage.content: A gallery operated by the Liberace Foundation that exhibits several of Liberace's cars including a mirrored Rolls Royce and rhinestone-studded Dusenberg. This exhibit comes from the now defunct Liberace Museum. Tour package can include transportation to and private viewing of the Liberace Museum Collection located inside Michael Jackson's home, Thriller Villa.

voyage.name: Area15
voyage.content: Just a hop away from The Strip, Area15 is an experiential entertainment amusement complex that has become a top Vegas destination since it opened at the end of 2019. Blacklights and fluorescent decorations abound to create an other-worldly gateway into alternate reality experiences. Open to all ages until 9PM.

voyage.name: Red Rock Canyon
voyage.price: Reservations required October through May. $20 per vehicle
voyage.content: Features a scenic drive through Red Rock Canyon, taking about 30 minutes to complete. There are opportunities to park up and get out of the car whether to take in the view, or get moving with a hike. Getting there without a car is hard, though organized bus tours do exist.

voyage.name: Cowabunga Canyon
voyage.content: Water park on the west side of town.

voyage.name: Machine Guns Vegas
voyage.content: Shooting range where you can use fully automatic weapons. Like many ranges in the Vegas area, they are tourist oriented, so interested foreigners to the US, or first-timers should not feel shy about dropping by and seeing what it's about.

voyage.name: Lockdown Escape Rooms - Sahara
voyage.content: Three themed rooms for 2-6 players: Pharaoh's Curse, Wrongfully Accused, and Cursed Cabin, all rated medium difficulty.

voyage.name: The Basement - A Live Escape Room Experience
voyage.content: Based on the original Basement in Los Angeles, this location has a pair of horror themed rooms that include the original Basement escape from a serial killer and a sequel called 'The Study'. One thing that sets the Basement apart from other escape rooms is the use of live actors in the experience.

voyage.name: VooDoo Zip Line
voyage.content: Las Vegas' second and highest zip line. The VooDoo zip line extends across the towers of the Rio Hotel and Casino where riders soar 400 feet in the air between the Rio's two towers, offering 360-degree open-air views of the Vegas valley.

voyage.name: Penn and Teller
voyage.content: Penn and Teller have been in showbusiness for nearly 30 years, and have kept their resident show at the Rio up to date throughout that time. A must-see for any fan of magic or comedy before the duo presumably retires in the upcoming years.

voyage.name: Chippendales
voyage.content: The original all male revue.

voyage.name: Las Vegas Aviators
voyage.content: A Triple-A baseball club, the Aviators have been in Las Vegas longer than any other professional sports team. The Aviators began as the Las Vegas Stars in 1983, changed their name to the Las Vegas 51s, a reference to Area 51, in 2001, and became the Aviators for 2019 and beyond. They have won 2 Pacific Coast League crowns and 10 division titles. The team opened a new ballpark in Summerlin in 2019.

voyage.name: College basketball tournaments
voyage.content: Of the four NCAA Division I conferences that hold their men's and women's basketball tournaments in the Las Vegas area, two of them hold those events at Orleans Arena, part of The Orleans hotel/casino complex. The West Coast Conference and Western Athletic Conference both hold their men's and women's tournaments in early March, with the winner of each tournament receiving its league's automatic berth in the NCAA men'

voyage.name: Las Vegas Raiders (NFL)
voyage.content: NFL (Football) team that began playing in Las Vegas in 2020 after relocating from Oakland.

voyage.name: UNLV Rebels (NCAA)
voyage.content: The new stadium is also home to the local Division I college football team, the UNLV Rebels. While most other UNLV teams play on their campus near Harry Reid Airport, the football team plays here. Uniquely, the Rebels play on an entirely different surface from the Raiders—the Rebels play on a permanently installed artificial surface, while the Raiders play on a grass field that slides in and out as needed.

voyage.name: Downtown Summerlin
voyage.content: Located in the western outskirts of Las Vegas, Downtown Summerlin offers 125 stores, restaurants and entertainment venues located in a 106-acre shopping district. Downtown Summerlin hosts 30 dining establishments and is in proximity of many other restaurants nearby as well as the Red Rock Casino. Plans exist to expand the area to 400 acres. Opened in 2014.

voyage.name: Monta Noodle House
voyage.price: $12 for a sizeable bowl of ramen
voyage.content: A small ramen shop along Spring Mountain Rd. serving authentic bowls of soup for cheap. A welcome reprieve from the prices that many may be used to paying on The Strip.

voyage.name: Zippy's
voyage.content: This sole mainland outpost of the much-loved Hawaiian plate lunch chain is a testament to Las Vegas' nickname of the "ninth island". In terms of the menu, fans of Zippy's know what to expect, including a wide variety of plate lunches and other Hawaiian specialties.

voyage.name: Frankie's Tiki Room
voyage.content: Authentic and pleasantly unpolished tiki bar with lots of great decor and potent drinks. Look for the pink neon sign.

voyage.name: Palace Station
voyage.content: A modest hotel that's part of the local Station Casinos chain, with lower rates and better games than those typical of Vegas hotels.

voyage.name: Gold Coast Hotel & Casino
voyage.content: A full service hotel with a casino, eight restaurants, a 70 lane bowling alley, 711 hotel rooms. Free shuttle to the Strip, free valet parking, fitness center. Views of the Strip.

voyage.name: The Orleans
voyage.content: A New Orleans French Quarter and Mardi Gras-themed casino. Affordable and family friendly. Includes an on-site arena that hosts the men's and women's basketball tournaments for the West Coast Conference and Western Athletic Conference every March.

voyage.name: Westgate Flamingo Bay
voyage.content: One and two bedroom villas equipped with a full kitchen, whirlpool tub, spacious living room and a fireplace. 2½ miles from the Strip.

voyage.name: Palms Casino Hotel & Palms Place
voyage.content: A great view of the Strip from the Ghostbar. A Maloof casino.

voyage.name: JW Marriott Las Vegas Resort and Spa
voyage.content: Resort that includes the 40,000 sq foot Aquae Sulis Spa & Salon.

voyage.name: Ethel M Chocolate Factory
voyage.price: Free. Chocolate tasting: Adult $25 (with wine $35), Student $20, Child under 10 $15 (kids under 6 discouraged from attending tasting)
voyage.content: Offers a free self-guided factory tour and has a large cactus garden. Chocolate tasting sessions, optionally with wine, by reservation. The Cactus Cafe has coffee, milkshakes, and brownies along with chocolate dipped fruit, pretzels, and marshmallows.

voyage.name: Clark County Museum
voyage.content: Historical exhibits include restored houses from various decades of Henderson's history.

voyage.name: Henderson Bird Viewing Preserve
voyage.content: Located within the Water Treatment Facility, this 140 acre preserve has nine ponds which attract migratory waterfowl and resident birds.

voyage.name: National Atomic Testing Museum
voyage.content: Artifacts, pictures, maps and video footage presenting nuclear weapons testing and development in the southwestern US. If you're interested in science and history it's definitely worth visiting, and it's also a great break if you've become tired of the Strip. Videography requires special permission.

voyage.name: U.S. Route 95 at night
voyage.content: This route climbs gradually northwest of Las Vegas so that the Strip's neon lights remain visible for a remarkably long distance, appearing as a luminous cloud from the furthest point.

voyage.name: Marjorie Barrick Museum of Art
voyage.price: Free, suggested donation $5 adults, $2 seniors and children

voyage.name: The Simpsons House
voyage.content: Full-size replica created to closely mimic the design of the cartoon house from The Simpsons. Given way in a 1997 contest by Fox and Pepsi, it's now a private residence.

voyage.name: The Gun Store
voyage.price: $250-400 for machine gun shoots; lower for other standard gun types
voyage.content: In addition to being a gun store, the range gives you a chance to shoot an automatic weapon. Photo ID required. Beware long lines. A 2-3 hour long wait is not unusual on weekends and busy days.

voyage.name: Pinball Hall of Fame
voyage.content: Old-style pinball machines and the newest ones from Stern are there, all in very good condition. Some favorite arcade games too. Definitely worth a look.

voyage.name: Maverick Helicopters
voyage.content: Helicopter tours that will take you over the Grand Canyon or above the neon lights and mega resorts of the Las Vegas Strip, as well as helicopter tours that include rafting down the Colorado River.

voyage.name: Number One Escape Room Las Vegas
voyage.content: The Number One Escape Room is a live escape room game. You have no tools except your wit and brains. You and your team of 2-5 people have 60 minutes to break out from one of six unique locked rooms.

voyage.name: UNLV Rebels
voyage.content: The athletic teams of the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, better known as UNLV, are popular in the area. The Rebels are members of the Mountain West Conference, which has been expanding and now has 12 members for football and 11 members for other sports. The most famous UNLV team is the men's basketball team, known as the "Runnin' Rebels"; though not as strong as in their heyday from the late 1970s through the early

voyage.name: Mountain West Conference basketball tournaments
voyage.content: Out of the four NCAA Division I conferences that hold their men's and women's basketball tournaments in the Las Vegas area, the MW is one of two that holds events in this part of town. The MW's men's and women's teams converge on the Thomas & Mack Center every March to determine the teams that will receive the league's automatic berths in the NCAA men's and women's tournaments.

voyage.name: Big West Conference basketball tournaments
voyage.address: Dollar Loan Center, 200 S. Green Valley Pkwy., Henderson
voyage.content: The other D-I conference that holds its tournaments in this area, the Big West has moved its men's and women's tournaments to the Dollar Loan Center in Henderson proper. The 2022 tournaments were the first events in the new arena.

voyage.name: National Finals Rodeo
voyage.content: The season-ending event of the annual Professional Rodeo Cowboys Association circuit is held over 10 days in December just off the Strip at the Thomas & Mack Center on the UNLV campus.

voyage.name: City of Henderson Recreation Centers
voyage.content: City of Henderson is home to a multitude of recreation centers with many amenities and activities ranging from indoor pools to archery classes. Prices Vary for passes and programs but if you're looking for a cheap way to have a lot of fun check out their website they have practically everything.

voyage.name: The District at Green Valley Ranch
Town Square
voyage.content: About half a mile south of Mandalay is an outdoor mall in the style of a small Mediterranean town that stands out amidst all the air-conditioned, indoor malls. The idea of open-air shopping in the summer in the desert might seem crazy at first, but an extensive network of trees, shadow alleys and water sprayers let you actually enjoy sunny afternoons outside. All shops and restaurants here have their own, distinguish

voyage.name: Las Vegas Premium Outlets South
voyage.content: 120 outlet stores in an indoor setting complete with two food courts.

voyage.name: Hofbräuhaus
voyage.content: The Hofbräuhaus replicates the world famous Bavarian Hofbräuhaus beer hall with festive German food and nightly entertainment. Patrons have an option of dining in the beer hall with live music in the evening or the quieter beer garden. Reservations recommended for quicker seating.

voyage.name: Envy Steakhouse
voyage.content: Inspired by Chef Richard Chamberlain, the menu includes premium quality, fresh ingredients from select purveyors around the country, featured in innovative dishes. Kobe filet, prime rib roast, black angus filet and prime bone-in rib eye. The walk-in wine cellar features 1,500 bottles of wine.

voyage.name: Bahama Breeze
voyage.content: Serves great tropical food. Large portions with a great atmosphere. Famous for their jerk chicken pasta, cinnamon mashed sweet potatoes, and wide variety of hand-crafted tropical drinks such as the Bahamarita. This is a great place to get away and relax from the crowds of people on the Strip.

voyage.name: Ellis Island Casino Restaurant
voyage.content: The $6.95 steak special is consistently voted one of the best deals in Las Vegas. It's not on the menu, so ask for it specifically. If steak is not your thing the restaurant has plenty of other selections at cheap prices. In addition, Ellis Island has barbecue every night from 4-10PM. Ellis Island also brews its own beer, and serves them in the casino bar in 20-oz glasses for $1.50.

voyage.name: Lawry's The Prime Rib
voyage.content: Juicy, succulent portions of the company namesake, Prime Rib. All prime rib dinners include original spinning bowl salad, Yorkshire pudding, mashed potatoes and whipped creamed horseradish. If you don't want prime rib (but why eat at a place called the Prime Rib if you don't want it?) there's always a ribeye steak available and a couple fish dishes.

voyage.name: Nobu
voyage.content: A staple for Las Vegas sushi lovers, newcomers will discover a fusion of traditional Japanese cuisine with Latin spices and flavors.

voyage.name: Double Down Saloon
voyage.content: Perhaps the finest dive bar in Vegas. A bit out of the way, but plenty of atmosphere.

voyage.name: Lovelady Brewing
voyage.hours: Mon 2-8PM, Tue-Thu 2-10PM, Fri Sat noon-11PM, Sun noon-8PM
voyage.content: 16 taps with weekly flavors. They have shuffleboard and cornhole, but no gambling. Non-smoking. Dogs allowed on outside patio. They sell snacks but you can bring in food.

voyage.name: Best Western Plus Henderson
voyage.content: 115 guest rooms and suites, each with a 32” flat panel television, microwave and mini refrigerator. Property amenities include a heated outdoor pool, 24-hour fitness center, free wireless internet, and a business center.

voyage.name: Residence Inn Las Vegas Henderson/Green Valley
Best Western Plus Las Vegas South Henderson
voyage.content: Plush accommodations, executive two-bedroom suites and flexible meeting space.

voyage.name: Arizona Charlie's Boulder
voyage.content: Casino hotel and RV park. Easy access from interstate and reasonable prices; great for overnight stays passing through Vegas. The lower floors of their sister property on the western side of Las Vegas, Arizona Charlie's Dacatur, may be one of the better options in the region for observant Jews who need a place to stay on the Sabbath.

voyage.name: Boulder Station
voyage.content: A modest hotel that's part of the local Station Casinos chain, with lower rates and better games than those typical of Vegas hotels.

voyage.name: Oasis Las Vegas RV Resort
voyage.content: Nice clean RV park south of the Strip, 50 amp full service hookups. Two pools and hot tubs. You'll need to drive or take a shuttle to the Strip. Easy access from I-15.

voyage.name: Sam's Town
voyage.content: Large motel property with considerable parking, including excellent facilities for RVs.

voyage.name: Thousand Trails Las Vegas RV Resort
voyage.content: Has swimming pool, spa, WiFi and laundry facilities.

voyage.name: Las Vegas KOA at Sam's Town
voyage.content: Campground located right by the Sam's Town Casino with numerous tent and RV sites available with 50 Max Amp full service hookups. Amenities include wi-fi, a pool/hot tub open year round, dog park, and a shuttle to the Las Vegas Strip.

voyage.name: Mardi Gras Hotel & Casino
voyage.content: Free complimentary shuttle service to the Strip.

voyage.name: Ellis Island Casino & Hotel
voyage.content: Has outdoor pool and two popular restaurants.

voyage.name: Hilton Grand Vacations Suites-Las Vegas (Convention Center)
voyage.content: Studios, one- & two-bedroom suites next to the Convention Center and monorail. Meeting space. Suites have full kitchens & washer/dryer.

voyage.name: Westgate Las Vegas Resort & Casino
voyage.content: This 3000-room hotel and casino is just north of the Las Vegas Convention Center, a couple of blocks east of the Strip. There is a monorail station is next to the lobby.

voyage.name: Las Vegas Marriott
voyage.content: The rooftop foyer presents beautiful sweeping views of the landscape.

voyage.name: Platinum Hotel
voyage.content: Boutique non-gaming hotel, all rooms are suites with kitchen and private balcony. Two blocks from the Strip.

voyage.name: Renaissance Las Vegas Hotel
voyage.content: Non-gaming, non-smoking hotel. No resort fees..

voyage.name: Embassy Suites by Hilton Las Vegas Convention Center
Residence Inn Las Vegas Hughes Center
voyage.content: Non-gaming, non-smoking hotel. No resort fees.

voyage.name: Hyatt Place Las Vegas
voyage.content: Popular for business travelers. 42" flat panel HDTV and free wi-fi in each room. Free breakfast and airport shuttle.

voyage.name: Virgin Hotels Las Vegas
voyage.content: An entertainment resort located on 16.7 acres on the corner of Harmon and Paradise Road, inside the Paradise Corridor.

voyage.name: West Wind Las Vegas 6 Drive-In
voyage.content: If time permits, and you don't mind watching a movie on your vacation, consider a visit to West Wind Drive-in; especially if visiting from out of the country where drive-ins are infrequent. And for an added bonus; it's normally a double-feature, so you get two movies for the price of one.

voyage.name: Nellis Air Force Base
voyage.content: Home base of the air demonstration squadron United States Air Force Thunderbirds among others, the base is open to the public during airshows. Other than that, you can see military aircraft taking off and landing from a distance.

voyage.name: Tule Springs Fossil Beds National Monument
voyage.content: For the more serious fossil bed hunter (see Floyd Lamb below for more accessible viewings).

voyage.name: Floyd Lamb Park
voyage.content: A pleasant oasis with ponds and tules and also the Tules Spring Ranch with some roaming peacocks and Pleistocene fossil exhibits.

voyage.name: Desert National Wildlife Refuge
voyage.content: Though not regularly visited, this is actually the largest national wildlife refuge in the lower 48 states. Coincidentally, it overlies part of the Nevada Test Site, so you can't just wander too willy-nilly, although the latter is quite distant. But this refuge's visitor center and trails will introduce you to aspects of the Mojave Desert ecosystem that are framed by some rather tall desert peaks, with a chance to se

voyage.name: Community College of Southern Nevada's Planetarium and Observatory
voyage.content: It's not on par with L.A.'s Griffith Observatory or Chicago's Adler Planetarium, but this planetarium and observatory can still help give an understanding to the skies and open space beyond. There's also an adjacent astronomy store that's open during the show times. Be aware, however, that chairs do not lean back, so there is a lot of looking up on your part.

voyage.name: Clark County Shooting Complex
voyage.hours: No public shooting Mon or Tue

voyage.name: Craig Ranch Regional Park
voyage.content: Skate and BMX park, sports fields and dog park. Includes the AMP, an outdoor amphitheater/ concert venue.

voyage.name: City of North Las Vegas Municipal Par 3 and Disc Golf Club
voyage.content: Golf and disc golf.

voyage.name: Las Vegas Motor Speedway
voyage.content: A 1200-acre complex of multiple tracks for automobile racing. The speedway also consists of a fan zone called The Neon Garage which has live entertainment, areas for fans to watch their favorite driver's car get worked on, and is home to the Winner's Circle.

voyage.name: NASCAR
voyage.content: Las Vegas hosts NASCAR for a weekend every year, usually in March. The race draws about 150,000 race fans to the city. Many cheer for Kurt and Kyle Busch, natives of Las Vegas. Aside from NASCAR, the speedway hosts many other racing events throughout the year.

voyage.name: Exotics Racing School
voyage.price: From $249 depending on the car and number of laps
voyage.content: After a training session, get behind the wheel of a Ferrari F430 F1 or other race car and go up to 130 mph with an instructor in the passenger seat.

voyage.name: Sun Buggy Fun Rentals
voyage.content: Dune buggy rentals and off-roading experiences at the Las Vegas dunes.

voyage.name: MRKT Sea & Land
voyage.content: Fine dining that features premium beef and poultry selections as well as seafood such as king crab, lobster, and scallops. MRKT also has one of North Las Vegas' most extensive wine lists.

voyage.name: Aliante Casino + Hotel
voyage.content: A casino-resort hotel and spa on the northern side of the Las Vegas valley along the northern beltway, about a 30-minute drive from the Strip and about 15 minutes from the Las Vegas Motor Speedway.

voyage.name: Hitchin' Post RV Park and Motel
voyage.content: Sites are cramped but cheap. They take your name but don't take reservations if they are nearly full (beware!).
